meta.title: Edged footprint: data centers in Caldwell County and Martindale, 14 days of posts
meta.subject: data centers, transmission and water in Caldwell County, Texas (Lockhart, Luling, Martindale, Maxwell, Hwy 142) — the Edged campus and other projects (Tract's Caldwell Valley Technology Park, code-named county projects), local opposition including the Caldwell Data Center Action Team, county and city oversight, tax abatements, Bluebonnet/LCRA power and groundwater use. STRICT RULE: a post must name or clearly concern Caldwell County, Lockhart, Luling, Martindale, Maxwell or these developers; anything else — statewide or national data center politics, Hays County or San Marcos with no Caldwell tie, other states, or Martindale in Indianapolis (Martindale-Brightwood) — is other
meta.subtitle: Oct 19 to Nov 1, 2026. Each dot is one post with 25+ views about data centers, power or water in Caldwell County or Martindale, plus every post repeating an earlier one, in the lane for what it argues. Higher and bigger means more views. White means 90% or more the same words as an earlier post, with a white line back to it. Coloured lines link a post to the post it quoted or replied to. Updated weekly.

lanes.label: Neighbors oppose (noise, land, quality of life)
lanes.description: Residents and local groups object to a data center near them — noise, lights, traffic, construction, property values, rural character or flooding — and organize to stop or delay it.

lanes.label: Water use and aquifers
lanes.description: Data centers will drain local water — aquifers, the San Marcos River, Plum Creek and Gonzales groundwater districts — or need cooling water the area can't spare.

lanes.label: Power, grid and transmission lines
lanes.description: Data center load strains the grid, raises power bills or brings new transmission lines and substations (Bluebonnet, LCRA, the Timmerman plant, ERCOT large-load queue).

lanes.label: Counties need authority over data centers
lanes.description: Caldwell County, Martindale, Lockhart or nearby cities say they need power to regulate data center siting — oversight motions, moratorium calls, permit notifications, asks to the Legislature.

lanes.label: Tax breaks and who pays
lanes.description: Abatements, tax incentives, campaign money and secrecy mean taxpayers and ratepayers subsidize developers; code-named deals hide who is behind a project.

lanes.label: Jobs, tax base and growth
lanes.description: Data center and infrastructure investment brings jobs, tax base and growth to Caldwell County, and the region should welcome it.

lanes.label: Pushback
lanes.description: Posts doubting, mocking, fact-checking or arguing against the dominant framings.

posts.text: San Marcos, Texas BANNED data centers within its city limits in June 2026, but a loophole was found—building the data center in Caldwell County, San Marcos’ neighbor. Although the data center will not be built directly in the city, it will still affect the city’s watershed.
